terms.definition: A push or a pull acting on an object.
terms.function: Can change an object's motion — start it, stop it, speed it up, or turn it.
terms.whereItIs: Drawn as arrows touching the box.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the single most common idea in physics, behind every machine and every movement.
One newton accelerates a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s²; it gives every force a measurable size.
terms.whereItIs: Read on the scale plate beside the box.

terms.definition: A force drawn as an arrow, length showing strength and heading showing direction.
terms.whyItMatters: The arrow is what lets opposite forces cancel and same-direction forces add.
terms.whereItIs: Every arrow in the scene, from the box surfaces.

terms.definition: The single leftover force after you add up (with direction) all forces on an object.
terms.whyItMatters: Only a non-zero net force changes motion; zero net force means no acceleration.
terms.whereItIs: The floating arrow above the box that appears during Go.
